timed_region: For each rank, the interval begins after the pre-computation MPI_Barrier and covers choleskyDecompositionDistributed plus waiting in the post-computation MPI_Barrier; the timer stops after that barrier.
start_synchronization: MPI_Barrier(g.world) precedes each rank's local start timestamp, but barrier returns need not be simultaneous. Rank 0 can record its start after another rank has already begun computation, so this does not establish a valid rank-0 global-makespan boundary.
stop_synchronization: The post-computation MPI_Barrier is entered only after each rank returns from the decomposition, so rank 0's subsequent stop timestamp cannot precede completion on another rank.
rank_aggregation: None. Every rank computes a local duration, but there is no MPI reduction or other aggregation of those durations.
reported_value: Only rank 0 prints its own duration.count() in milliseconds as "Computation time".
semantic_equivalence_basis: The rank-0 interval is not demonstrably equivalent to the maximum per-rank elapsed time. Although its stop follows global completion, its start may occur after relevant work has begun on another rank. The source neither reduces local durations with MPI_MAX nor otherwise proves that rank 0's reported interval encloses the full parallel makespan.

evidence.finding: All ranks pass through a barrier, take separate local start timestamps, execute the distributed decomposition, pass through a second barrier, and take separate local stop timestamps.
The canonical output is emitted only by rank 0 and uses that rank's local duration directly.
Result gathering and validation are conditional and occur after the canonical time is printed; disabling validation does not introduce any missing timing aggregation or alternate timer.

minimal_fix: After computing each rank's elapsed duration, use MPI_Reduce or MPI_Allreduce with MPI_MAX and a matching datatype, then print the resulting maximum on rank 0. The existing per-rank intervals may be reduced as-is, although moving each local stop immediately after the decomposition would exclude the post-computation barrier wait.
notes: The post-computation barrier makes each local interval complete but does not turn rank 0's interval into the maximum. Millisecond truncation is ordinary display precision and is not itself a defect.

timed_region: Each rank starts its own clock after the initial MPI_Barrier, executes the complete floydWarshall call, enters a final MPI_Barrier, and stops its clock after returning from that barrier (floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp:281-288). The interval includes distribution, CUDA allocation and transfers, kernels, device completion, result gathering, deallocation, and final synchronization.
start_synchronization: MPI_Barrier precedes the per-rank start calls, but barrier returns are not simultaneous. A non-root rank can take its timestamp and begin timed work, including local matrix allocation, before rank 0 takes the timestamp used for the canonical result. Thus rank 0's start is not proven to precede all timed work.
stop_synchronization: Adequate. cudaDeviceSynchronize completes queued GPU kernels, subsequent device-to-host copies and gathers are blocking, and every rank completes the function before entering the final barrier. Rank 0 takes its stop timestamp only after that barrier returns, so all ranks have completed the relevant work.
rank_aggregation: There is no reduction or other aggregation of the independently measured rank durations. Only rank 0's local duration is retained for reporting.
reported_value: The canonical label prints rank 0's duration.count() in milliseconds, not MPI_MAX of all rank durations or a proven equivalent global makespan. The millisecond unit conversion itself is correct.
semantic_equivalence_basis: No global-makespan equivalence is established. The final barrier gives rank 0 a globally enclosing stop, but the initial barrier does not make rank 0's start precede other ranks' timed work. Work also varies by rank through unequal row blocks, pivot-row ownership, and root-only gather responsibilities, so rank 0's unaggregated interval is not guaranteed to be the maximum.

evidence.finding: Each rank independently timestamps after an MPI_Barrier and stops after another MPI_Barrier; neither elapsed value is aggregated.
Timed work begins with rank-local vector construction before the first Scatterv, so another rank can begin its timed region before rank 0 records the start used for output.
Ranks perform differing work according to row ownership and pivot ownership, including owner-only pivot-row device-to-host copies.
GPU work is explicitly synchronized before blocking copies and gathers; the function completes these operations and CUDA deallocation before returning.
After the final barrier, rank 0 prints only its own local duration as "Computation time".
Result printing and validation occur after the benchmark timer; validation mode does not supply a different timed computation path or repair the missing aggregation.

minimal_fix: After every rank computes its local elapsed time, apply MPI_Reduce (or MPI_Allreduce) with MPI_MAX using a matching numeric datatype, and have rank 0 print that maximum under "Computation time". The existing complete per-rank timed intervals and device synchronization can otherwise remain unchanged.
notes: The final result gathering and CUDA teardown are included in the timer, which may make the measurement conservatively slower but is not itself a validity defect. No missing device synchronization or timer-unit error is present.

timed_region: On every rank, MPI_Wtime starts after the barrier at floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp:185 and stops after the final barrier at lines 222-223. The interval includes the complete distributed Floyd-Warshall loop at lines 188-220 and final synchronization, but excludes setup, initial host-to-device transfers, result copies, gathering, and cleanup.
start_synchronization: MPI_Barrier precedes each rank's local start at lines 185-186. This does not make rank 0's start provably no later than work on every other rank because barrier returns need not be simultaneous.
stop_synchronization: Each CUDA kernel stream is synchronized at line 217, and all ranks enter an MPI_Barrier at line 222 before taking tEnd at line 223. Thus accelerator work and relevant computation on every rank have completed before rank 0 stops.
rank_aggregation: None. Every rank returns its own tEnd - tStart at line 246; there is no MPI_MAX reduction or other aggregation of these elapsed durations.
reported_value: Rank 0 converts its own rank-local elapsedSeconds to milliseconds and prints it as "Computation time" at lines 391-393.
semantic_equivalence_basis: No equivalent global makespan is proved. Although the stop barrier ensures rank 0 stops after all ranks finish, rank 0 starts its timer only after returning from the initial barrier and may start after another rank has already begun timed work. Consequently its local interval can be shorter than the maximum complete per-rank elapsed duration.

evidence.finding: All ranks execute a barrier and then independently record their local start time; the barrier does not guarantee simultaneous return.
The timed computation is the full distributed Floyd-Warshall loop on every rank.
Every launched GPU update is followed by cudaStreamSynchronize, so asynchronous kernel work completes within each rank's timed interval.
A final MPI barrier ensures all ranks have completed the loop before each rank records its local stop time.
The function returns only the calling rank's local elapsed duration.
No rank aggregation occurs after the distributed call; rank 0 prints its own elapsedSeconds as the canonical Computation time.

minimal_fix: After computing each rank's local elapsed duration, reduce it with MPI_Reduce using MPI_MAX and MPI_DOUBLE to rank 0, then use that reduced maximum for the canonical Computation time and performance calculation.
notes: The millisecond conversion is dimensionally correct, and truncation to whole milliseconds is ordinary display precision rather than a timer-unit defect.
